court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Additional Sessions Judge-1, Nanded in Special (POSCO) Case No.6/2013
case_name: Maroti @ Banaji S/O Anandrao Zalke vs The State Of Maharashtra
facts_of_case: Prosecutrix filed F.I.R. claiming accused pressed her mouth and grappled with her; trial court convicted accused under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and fine of Rs.5000/-; present appeal.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to prove that the victim's testimony is unreliable.
legal_principles.held: According to the counsel, the victim deserves to be disbelieved as initially she made grievance only under Section 354 of the IPC, but later on, on the same day she went on to claim that she had actually been raped.

legal_principles.principle: The victim's testimony can be corroborated by medical evidence and the evidence of other witnesses.
legal_principles.held: However, trial Court found that the victim was sufficiently corroborated by medical evidence and the evidence of P.W.2 Panchfulabai and P.W.3 Yashoda.
